fact.claim: XEQT's own September 2026 iShares fact sheet puts the United States at 45.79% of the fund as at 30-Sep-2026, and Vanguard lists VFV at 100.00% United States as at Sep 30 2026. Hold 80% XEQT and 20% VFV and the US share goes from 45.79% to about 56.6%, a jump of roughly 11 percentage points; at 50/50 it is about 72.9%, a jump of about 27 points. XEQT's US sleeve is two total-US-market iShares funds worth 45.77% of the portfolio between them, so every S&P 500 company VFV buys is already inside XEQT — the split changes weights, it does not add new companies. The condition worth saying out loud: the extra weight lands on the biggest US names first, with NVIDIA alone at 8.37038% of VFV, so this is a concentration decision, not diversification.

plain.what: XEQT is one fund that holds many companies at once. Its own September 2026 fact sheet says 45.79% of it is already United States companies. VFV is another fund that is 100.00% United States, so adding it moves how much of your money sits in the US — it does not add any new companies you didn't already own.
plain.so_what: If you held 80% XEQT and 20% VFV, your US share would go from 45.79% to about 56.6% — roughly 11 percentage points more riding on one country.
plain.do: Open your fund page today and write down the US percentage it shows, instead of guessing from memory.
